feature_contract.goal: Preserve the entire R23 DirectGPU host sample freshness decision from the original seqlock publication through millisecond age conversion and safe stale/invalid fallback even after long uptime and with extremely high QPC frequencies.
feature_contract.scope_boundary: Only R23 host freshness QPC conversion and its pure C++ regression tests; no semantic HUD, outer lens flare, SkyGlow, FFB, world stereo, DX11 or DXVK changes.
feature_contract.special_work_evidence: Pre-fix R23 multiplied arbitrary nonnegative QPC delta by 1000 in signed int64 and overflowed after days at GHz frequencies; the first candidate also used floating point above INT64_MAX/1000, which can round a below-boundary age upward on MSVC's 64-bit long double and alter stale/fresh decisions.
trace_stages: Host XR frame seqlock publishes latest DirectGPU host sampleQpc/frequency/transport status.
R23DiagnoseHostFreshness validates host flags, current QPC monotonicity and computes signed age milliseconds without QPC integer overflow.
Stale/invalid/fresh classification chooses safe transport fallback while preserving existing OpenXR binocular frame and device-reset behavior.
subcomponents: Replace R23 signed elapsedTicks*1000 conversion with saturation-safe whole-seconds plus exact fractional remainder path.
Keep common QPC age arithmetic one integer multiply/divide; avoid floating-point rounding near millisecond decision boundaries for the extreme-frequency case.
Cover zero/negative/disordered clocks, multi-day high-frequency ages, exact boundaries, saturation and destructive verifier cases through C++ and Python smoke.

acceptance_items.expected_behavior: R23 exact millisecond age is monotonic and free from overflow or floating-point boundary rounding before stale/fresh selection.
Invalid QPC order/frequency preserves qpc-invalid fallback; long stale samples do not become fresh, and QPC values saturate safely.
Exact validation-bearing SHA must pass full DX9Ex Active Win32 x86 game/x64 host/package, Domain Isolation, and Full Source Impact when applicable.

diagnosis.original_evidence: At material 7119ed3 R23 originally converted (now-sample)*1000 in signed 64-bit; run 38537820149 then failed policy on absent 00834 run record before compilation. The first R23 QPC helper still used floating-point fallback for huge frequencies.
source_trace: XR R23 host shared QPC publication/flags and seqlock snapshot
R23 frame routing evaluates sample-stale versus qpc-invalid versus fresh before XR display
diagnosis.root_cause: Multiplying elapsed QPC ticks by 1000 overflows long-uptime 64-bit math; the initial high-frequency fallback uses long double, which has 53-bit mantissa on MSVC and may round an age just below millisecond boundary upward.
alternatives_rejected: Floating-point multiplication is not exact on 64-bit long double implementations at 9e18 tick frequencies.
Always iterating 1000 modular additions would degrade normal per-Present QPC path; only the extraordinary branch uses bounded iteration.
diagnosis.fix_evidence: Existing integer quotient/remainder protects ordinary and multi-day QPC. Additional extraordinary-frequency modular accumulation preserves floor(remainder*1000/frequency) without overflow or floating-point rounding.
diagnosis.negative_test_evidence: Standalone C++20 -fsanitize=undefined and -Werror smoke passed full old cases plus 9e18 Hz below/exact 2ms boundary; GitHub exact-SHA smoke and verifier remain pending.
